findings.summary: The figure's meaning now sits where a reader can see it, but the embedding still gives it only an alt attribute and no visible caption: the page reads , so the one sentence that states what the four rows have in common exists only for assistive technology and never appears beside the picture. This no longer blocks a sighted reader, because every row in the rendered PNG now carries its own state title, its own note in the right-hand column and a keyed legend, but a one-line caption under the image would state the comparison once instead of leaving the reader to assemble it from four rows.

rubric_verdicts.contrast: pass - the row titles render in near-black #1a1a1a (about 17:1 on white), the right-hand notes and grey legend entries in #5f5f5f (about 6.0:1) and the blue legend entries in #2f6fa8 (about 5.3:1), all on plain white, and the grey seat fill #929292 clears about 3.1:1 so each seat reads as data.
rubric_verdicts.data_ink: pass - the seat blocks and the four seat states carry the visual weight; the only other ink is the titles, keyed legends and the four short notes that decode the states, and no gradient, shadow or decorative fill is drawn.
rubric_verdicts.decoration: pass - the canvas is plain white with flat grey #929292 blocks (one blue fill, one black outline, one blue outline) and flat text; nothing competes with the seats.
rubric_verdicts.label_collision: pass - no text is clipped: all ink lies between x 60 and x 1277 of the 1400 px canvas and y 53 to y 696 of 720. No label overlaps another label or the seat grid: the left titles and legends end by x 630, the grid ends at x 623 and the right-hand notes start at x 698, and row 2's arrow sits below its seat rather than on it.
rubric_verdicts.legibility: pass - each of the four rows now names its state in a title ("roster at its cap", "one seat frees", "one seat free, nothing on another lane waiting", "one seat free, a named request waiting"), the right-hand column states the consequence of each, and a keyed blue legend plus the label "named lane request launches" under row 2 identify the conventions; a reader can decode which waiting request takes the freed seat from the picture alone.
rubric_verdicts.table_form: pass - four roster states across eight seats is a state comparison in which the position of the differing seat is the information, so the picture form carries it better than a table of occupied/empty cells would.
